methods.name: Stage-Progression
methods.rationale: Applies typical Series C → next-stage step-up multiplier (1.7x) to $380M total raised proxy.

methods.name: Peer-Median
methods.skip_reason: insufficient narrow peer set in Transportation (found 0 same-stage, 0 adjacent-stage, 0 similar-tier; need ≥3)
methods.rationale: 3 same-sector peers exist in Transportation, but none of the narrow filters (same-stage / adjacent-stage / similar-valuation-tier) yielded ≥3 datapoints. Falling back to all-sector median would be misleading.

data.narrative:
ZeroAvia is a Series C transportation company founded by Valery Miftakhov that has raised $380M+ to date. The broader transportation sector includes 8 private peers (Rivian, The Boring Company, Einride, Slate Auto, Harbinger, and others) and no public comparables, limiting traditional peer-median triangulation.

Given the lack of same-stage or adjacent-stage peers meeting minimum sample size (3+), peer-median valuation was not applicable. Instead, stage-progression methodology was deployed, using the $380M total raised as a proxy base and applying a 1.7x step-up multiplier typical of Series C to subsequent-stage advancement. This yields an implied valuation of $646M.

The analysis supports a valuation range of $549M to $743M, with a median point estimate of $646M. Key uncertainties center on the strength of the 1.7x multiplier assumption in a frontier transportation subsector where market comparables are sparse and fundraising dynamics may diverge from historical venture norms. Validation of this range would benefit from clarity on ZeroAvia's unit economics, path to profitability, and regulatory milestones for hydrogen-electric propulsion in regional aviation.
